sanskrit: tata āśliṣya sa premṇā mūrdhni cāghrāya pāṇḍavam prītyā paramayā yuktaḥ prasmayaṃś cābravīj jayam
english: Then, embracing the son of Pāṇḍu lovingly and kissing him upon the head, filled with the highest affection and smiling, he spoke to the Conqueror:

sanskrit: karṇena me mahābāho sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ kavacaṃ ca dhvajaś caiva dhanuḥ śaktir hayā gadā śaraiḥ kṛttā maheṣvāsa yatamānasya saṃyuge
english: "O mighty-armed one, before the eyes of the whole army Karṇa cut down with his arrows my armor, my banner, my bow, my spear, my horses, and my mace, O great archer, even as I strove in the battle.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ jñātvā raṇe tasya karma dṛṣṭvā ca phalguna vyavasīdāmi duḥkhena na ca me jīvitaṃ priyam
english: Having known and seen his prowess in battle, O Phalguna, I sink down in grief, and life itself is no longer dear to me.

sanskrit: tam adya yadi vai vīra na haniṣyasi sūtajam prāṇān eva parityakṣye jīvitārtho hi ko mama
english: O hero, if today you do not slay that son of a charioteer, I shall abandon my very breath of life — for what use have I of living?"

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ pratyuvāca vijayo bharatarṣabha satyena te śape rājan prasādena tavaiva ca bhīmena ca naraśreṣṭha yamābhyāṃ ca mahīpate
english: Thus addressed, the Ever-Victorious replied, O bull of the Bhāratas: "By truth I swear to you, O king, and by your own favor, and by Bhīma, O best of men, and by the twins, O lord of the earth —

sanskrit: yathādya samare karṇaṃ haniṣyāmi hato 'tha vā mahītale patiṣyāmi satyenāyudham ālabhe
english: that this very day in battle I shall slay Karṇa, or else, slain, I shall fall upon the earth. By truth I lay my hand upon my weapon."

sanskrit: evam ābhāṣya rājānam abravīn mādhavaṃ vacaḥ adya karṇaṃ raṇe kṛṣṇa sūdayiṣye na saṃśayaḥ tad anudhyāhi bhadraṃ te vadhaṃ tasya durātmanaḥ
english: Having spoken thus to the king, he addressed these words to Mādhava: "This day in battle I shall slay Karṇa, O Kṛṣṇa — there is no doubt. Set your mind, may you prosper, upon the death of that evil-souled one."

sanskrit: evam ukto 'bravīt pārthaṃ keśavo rājasattama śakto 'smi bharataśreṣṭha yatnaṃ kartuṃ yathābalam
english: Thus addressed, Keśava said to Pārtha, O best of kings: "I am able, O best of the Bhāratas, to make every effort according to my strength.

sanskrit: evaṃ cāpi hi me kāmo nityam eva mahāratha kathaṃ bhavān raṇe karṇaṃ nihanyād iti me matiḥ
english: And this too has ever been my desire, O great chariot-warrior; my thought is always how you might slay Karṇa in battle."

sanskrit: bhūyaś covāca matimān mādhavo dharmanandanam yudhiṣṭhiremaṃ bībhatsuṃ tvaṃ sāntvayitum arhasi anujñātuṃ ca karṇasya vadhāyādya durātmanaḥ
english: And the wise Mādhava spoke further to the son of Dharma: "Yudhiṣṭhira, you should soothe this Bībhatsu, and grant him leave today for the slaying of the evil-souled Karṇa.

sanskrit: śrutvā hy ayam ahaṃ caiva tvāṃ karṇaśarapīḍitam pravṛttiṃ jñātum āyātāv iha pāṇḍavanandana
english: For having heard that you were tormented by Karṇa's arrows, both he and I came here to learn how things stood, O joy of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: diṣṭyāsi rājan nirujo diṣṭyā na grahaṇaṃ gataḥ parisāntvaya bībhatsuṃ jayam āśādhi cānagha
english: By good fortune, O king, you are free of hurt; by good fortune you were not taken captive. Console Bībhatsu, and bid the Conqueror to victory, O sinless one."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ehy ehi pārtha bībhatso māṃ pariṣvaja pāṇḍava vaktavyam ukto 'smy ahitaṃ tvayā kṣāntaṃ ca tan mayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Come, come, O Pārtha, Bībhatsu, embrace me, son of Pāṇḍu. I was told by you what ought to have been said, though it was harsh — and that I have forgiven.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvām anujānāmi jahi karṇaṃ dhanaṃjaya manyuṃ ca mā kṛthāḥ pārtha yan mayokto 'si dāruṇam
english: I grant you leave — slay Karṇa, O Dhanaṃjaya. And bear no anger, O Pārtha, for the cruel words I spoke to you."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato dhanaṃjayo rājañ śirasā praṇatas tadā pādau jagrāha pāṇibhyāṃ bhrātur jyeṣṭhasya māriṣa
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Dhanaṃjaya, O king, bowing with his head, clasped with both hands the feet of his eldest brother, O venerable one.

sanskrit: samutthāpya tato rājā pariṣvajya ca pīḍitam mūrdhny upāghrāya caivainam idaṃ punar uvāca ha
english: Then the king, raising him up and embracing him close, and kissing him upon the head, spoke to him once more these words:

sanskrit: dhanaṃjaya mahābāho mānito 'smi dṛḍhaṃ tvayā māhātmyaṃ vijayaṃ caiva bhūyaḥ prāpnuhi śāśvatam
english: "O mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya, you have honored me well. May you attain greatness and victory once more, and that everlasting."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca adya taṃ pāpakarmāṇaṃ sānubandhaṃ raṇe śaraiḥ nayāmy antaṃ samāsādya rādheyaṃ balagarvitam
english: Arjuna said: "This day, closing with that evil-doing Rādheya, proud of his strength, together with his kinsmen, I shall bring him to his end in battle with my arrows.

sanskrit: yena tvaṃ pīḍito bāṇair dṛḍham āyamya kārmukam tasyādya karmaṇaḥ karṇaḥ phalaṃ prāpsyati dāruṇam
english: He by whom you were tormented with arrows, drawing his bow taut — for that deed Karṇa shall this day reap a terrible fruit.

sanskrit: adya tvām aham eṣyāmi karṇaṃ hatvā mahīpate sabhājayitum ākrandād iti satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: This day, having slain Karṇa, O lord of the earth, I shall come to you to do you honor amid the cries of war — this I tell you truly.

sanskrit: nāhatvā vinivarte 'haṃ karṇam adya raṇājirāt iti satyena te pādau spṛśāmi jagatīpate
english: I shall not turn back from the field of battle this day without having slain Karṇa — and on this truth I touch your feet, O lord of the world."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca prasādya dharmarājānaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā pārthaḥ provāca govindaṃ sūtaputravadhodyataḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having won over the King of Righteousness, Pārtha, with gladdened inmost heart and bent upon the slaying of the charioteer's son, spoke to Govinda:

sanskrit: kalpyatāṃ ca ratho bhūyo yujyantāṃ ca hayottamāḥ āyudhāni ca sarvāṇi sajjyantāṃ vai mahārathe
english: "Let the chariot be made ready once more, and let the finest horses be yoked, and let all the weapons be set in order upon the great car.

sanskrit: upāvṛttāś ca turagāḥ śikṣitāś cāśvasādinaḥ rathopakaraṇaiḥ sarvair upāyāntu tvarānvitāḥ
english: Let the well-trained horses and the skilled horsemen, with all the gear of the chariot, come forth in haste."

sanskrit: evam ukte mahārāja phalgunena mahātmanā uvāca dārukaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kuru sarvaṃ yathābravīt arjuno bharataśreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: When this was spoken, O great king, by the high-souled Phalguna, Kṛṣṇa said to Dāruka: "Do all as Arjuna, best of the Bhāratas, foremost of all bowmen, has said."

sanskrit: ājñaptas tv atha kṛṣṇena dāruko rājasattama yojayām āsa sa rathaṃ vaiyāghraṃ śatrutāpanam
english: Then, commanded by Kṛṣṇa, Dāruka, O best of kings, yoked that tiger-skinned chariot, the scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ tu ratham āsthāya dārukeṇa mahātmanā āpṛcchya dharmarājānaṃ brāhmaṇān svasti vācya ca samaṅgalasvastyayanam āruroha rathottamam
english: Mounting the chariot now yoked by the high-souled Dāruka, taking leave of the King of Righteousness and bidding the brāhmaṇas pronounce their blessings, amid auspicious benedictions he ascended that finest of chariots.

sanskrit: tasya rājā mahāprājño dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ āśiṣo 'yuṅkta paramā yuktāḥ karṇavadhaṃ prati
english: Upon him the king, the deeply wise Yudhiṣṭhira, the Lord of Righteousness, bestowed the highest blessings, fit for the slaying of Karṇa.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūtāni bhārata nihataṃ menire karṇaṃ pāṇḍavena mahātmanā
english: Seeing that great archer setting forth, O Bhārata, the creatures reckoned Karṇa already slain by the high-souled son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: babhūvur vimalāḥ sarvā diśo rājan samantataḥ cāṣāś ca śatapatrāś ca krauñcāś caiva janeśvara pradakṣiṇam akurvanta tadā vai pāṇḍunandanam
english: All the quarters grew clear on every side, O king; and blue jays and woodpeckers and herons, O lord of men, then circled rightward about the joy of the Pāṇḍus.

sanskrit: bahavaḥ pakṣiṇo rājan puṃnāmānaḥ śubhāḥ śivāḥ tvarayanto 'rjunaṃ yuddhe hṛṣṭarūpā vavāśire
english: Many birds, O king, bearing masculine names, auspicious and benign, urging Arjuna on to battle, cried out in joyful guise.

sanskrit: kaṅkā gṛdhrā vaḍāś caiva vāyasāś ca viśāṃ pate agratas tasya gacchanti bhakṣyahetor bhayānakāḥ
english: Herons, vultures, cranes, and crows, O lord of peoples, went on before him, fearsome, in their craving for flesh.

sanskrit: nimittāni ca dhanyāni pārthasya praśaśaṃsire vināśam arisainyānāṃ karṇasya ca vadhaṃ tathā
english: And the auspicious omens proclaimed for Pārtha the destruction of the enemy's host and the slaying of Karṇa as well.

sanskrit: prayātasyātha pārthasya mahān svedo vyajāyata cintā ca vipulā jajñe kathaṃ nv etad bhaviṣyati
english: Then, as Pārtha set forth, a great sweat broke upon him, and a deep anxiety arose: "How indeed will this come to pass?"

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvadhanvānam abravīn madhusūdanaḥ dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ tadāyastaṃ cintāparigataṃ tadā
english: Then the Slayer of Madhu, seeing Pārtha strained and gripped by anxiety, spoke to the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva:

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvadhanvan saṃgrāme ye tvayā dhanuṣā jitāḥ na teṣāṃ mānuṣo jetā tvad anya iha vidyate
english: "O wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, of those whom you have vanquished in battle with your bow, there is no human conqueror to be found here other than you.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā hi bahavaḥ śūrāḥ śakratulyaparākramāḥ tvāṃ prāpya samare vīraṃ ye gatāḥ paramāṃ gatim
english: For many heroes have been seen, in valor equal to Śakra, who, meeting you in battle, O hero, have gone to the highest goal.

sanskrit: ko hi droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca bhagadattaṃ ca māriṣa vindānuvindāv āvantyau kāmbojaṃ ca sudakṣiṇam
english: For who, O venerable one, could stand against Droṇa and Bhīṣma and Bhagadatta, and Vinda and Anuvinda of Avanti, and Sudakṣiṇa of the Kāmbojas,

sanskrit: śrutāyuṣaṃ mahāvīryam acyutāyuṣam eva ca pratyudgamya bhavet kṣemī yo na syāt tvam iva kṣamī
english: and the mighty Śrutāyus, and Acyutāyus too, and emerge unharmed — who is there so capable as you?

sanskrit: tava hy astrāṇi divyāni lāghavaṃ balam eva ca vedhaḥ pātaś ca lakṣaś ca yogaś caiva tavārjuna asaṃmohaś ca yuddheṣu vijñānasya ca saṃnatiḥ
english: For yours are the celestial weapons, and lightness of hand, and strength; yours, O Arjuna, the piercing, the casting, the aim, and the union of all; and freedom from bewilderment in battle, and the bending of all knowledge to your will.

sanskrit: bhavān devāsurān sarvān hanyāt sahacarācarān pṛthivyāṃ hi raṇe pārtha na yoddhā tvatsamaḥ pumān
english: You could slay all the gods and demons together with all that moves and moves not; for upon the earth, O Pārtha, there is no warrior, no man, equal to you in battle.

sanskrit: dhanurgrahā hi ye ke cit kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ ā devāt tvatsamaṃ teṣāṃ na paśyāmi śṛṇomi vā
english: For of all the bow-wielding warriors, mad with the lust of battle, from the gods downward, I neither see nor hear of one equal to you.

sanskrit: brahmaṇā ca prajāḥ sṛṣṭā gāṇḍīvaṃ ca mahādbhutam yena tvaṃ yudhyase pārtha tasmān nāsti tvayā samaḥ
english: By Brahmā were the creatures created, and so too the marvelous Gāṇḍīva with which you fight, O Pārtha; therefore there is none equal to you.

sanskrit: avaśyaṃ tu mayā vācyaṃ yat pathyaṃ tava pāṇḍava māvamaṃsthā mahābāho karṇam āhavaśobhinam
english: Yet I must surely tell you what is wholesome for you, O son of Pāṇḍu: do not, O mighty-armed one, hold lightly Karṇa, who shines in battle.

sanskrit: karṇo hi balavān dhṛṣṭaḥ kṛtāstraś ca mahārathaḥ kṛtī ca citrayodhī ca deśe kāle ca kovidaḥ
english: For Karṇa is strong and bold, accomplished in arms and a great chariot-warrior, skilled and a wondrous fighter, expert in place and time.

sanskrit: tejasā vahnisadṛśo vāyuvegasamo jave antakapratimaḥ krodhe siṃhasaṃhanano balī
english: In splendor he is like fire, in swiftness equal to the wind's rush, in wrath the very likeness of Death, with the frame of a lion, and mighty.

sanskrit: ayoratnir mahābāhur vyūḍhoraskaḥ sudurjayaḥ atimānī ca śūraś ca pravīraḥ priyadarśanaḥ
english: With arms long as iron bars, mighty-armed, broad-chested, hard to conquer, exceedingly proud, valiant, a foremost hero, and fair to look upon.

sanskrit: sarvair yodhaguṇair yukto mitrāṇām abhayaṃkaraḥ satataṃ pāṇḍavadveṣī dhārtarāṣṭrahite rataḥ
english: Endowed with every warrior's virtue, a giver of safety to his friends, ever a hater of the Pāṇḍavas, and devoted to the welfare of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: sarvair avadhyo rādheyo devair api savāsavaiḥ ṛte tvām iti me buddhis tvam adya jahi sūtajam
english: Rādheya is, to my mind, one who cannot be slain by all the gods together with Vāsava — save by you. This day, then, slay the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: devair api hi saṃyattair bibhradbhir māṃsaśoṇitam aśakyaḥ samare jetuṃ sarvair api yuyutsubhiḥ
english: Even by the gods arrayed for war, bearing flesh and blood, all of them eager to fight, he cannot be conquered in battle.

sanskrit: durātmānaṃ pāpamatiṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ; duṣṭaprajñaṃ pāṇḍaveyeṣu nityam hīnasvārthaṃ pāṇḍaveyair virodhe; hatvā karṇaṃ dhiṣṭhitārtho bhavādya
english: Slaying that evil-souled one, wicked-minded and cruel, of corrupt understanding, ever set against the sons of Pāṇḍu, and forsaking his own good in his enmity with the Pāṇḍavas — by slaying Karṇa this day, become one whose purpose is fulfilled.

sanskrit: vīraṃ manyata ātmānaṃ yena pāpaḥ suyodhanaḥ tam adya mūlaṃ pāpānāṃ jaya sautiṃ dhanaṃjaya
english: He through whom the wicked Suyodhana deems himself a hero — that son of a charioteer, the root of all these evils, conquer this day, O Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ punar ameyātmā keśavo 'rjunam abravīt kṛtasaṃkalpam āyastaṃ vadhe karṇasya sarvaśaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then again the immeasurable-souled Keśava spoke to Arjuna, who was resolved and wholly intent upon the slaying of Karṇa:

sanskrit: adya saptadaśāhāni vartamānasya bhārata vināśasyātighorasya naravāraṇavājinām
english: "This day, O Bhārata, the seventeenth day is passing of that most dreadful destruction of men and elephants and horses.

sanskrit: bhūtvā hi vipulā senā tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha anyonyaṃ samare prāpya kiṃciccheṣā viśāṃ pate
english: Vast though the army of your kinsmen was, closing with the foe in mutual battle, but little of it now remains, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: bhūtvā hi kauravāḥ pārtha prabhūtagajavājinaḥ tvāṃ vai śatruṃ samāsādya vinaṣṭā raṇamūrdhani
english: For the Kauravas, O Pārtha, abounding in elephants and horses, having met you as their foe, were destroyed at the head of battle.

sanskrit: ete ca sarve pāñcālāḥ sṛñjayāś ca sahānvayāḥ tvāṃ samāsādya durdharṣaṃ pāṇḍavāś ca vyavasthitāḥ
english: And all these Pāñcālas and Sṛñjayas with their kindred, and the Pāṇḍavas, having gained you, the unassailable, stand firm.

sanskrit: pāñcālaiḥ pāṇḍavair matsyaiḥ kārūṣaiś cedikekayaiḥ tvayā guptair amitraghna kṛtaḥ śatrugaṇakṣayaḥ
english: By the Pāñcālas, the Pāṇḍavas, the Matsyas, the Karūṣas, the Cedis and the Kekayas, guarded by you, O slayer of foes, was the host of enemies brought to ruin.

sanskrit: ko hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ kauravāṃs tāta saṃgatān anyatra pāṇḍavān yuddhe tvayā guptān mahārathān
english: For who, dear one, is able to conquer in battle the Kauravas gathered together, save the Pāṇḍavas, those great chariot-warriors, when guarded by you in war?

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi śakto raṇe jetuṃ sasurāsuramānuṣān trīṃl lokān samam udyuktān kiṃ punaḥ kauravaṃ balam
english: For you are able in battle to conquer the three worlds with their gods, demons, and men, all together arrayed — how much more, then, the host of the Kauravas?

sanskrit: bhagadattaṃ hi rājānaṃ ko 'nyaḥ śaktas tvayā vinā jetuṃ puruṣaśārdūla yo 'pi syād vāsavopamaḥ
english: For King Bhagadatta, O tiger among men, who else but you was able to conquer — even were he the equal of Vāsava?

sanskrit: tathemāṃ vipulāṃ senāṃ guptāṃ pārtha tvayānagha na śekuḥ pārthivāḥ sarve cakṣurbhir abhivīkṣitum
english: And this vast army guarded by you, O sinless Pārtha — all the kings of the earth could not even look upon it with their eyes.

sanskrit: tathaiva satataṃ pārtha rakṣitābhyāṃ tvayā raṇe dhṛṣṭadyumnaśikhaṇḍibhyāṃ bhīṣmadroṇau nipātitau
english: And likewise, O Pārtha, by Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, ever guarded by you in battle, were Bhīṣma and Droṇa brought down.

sanskrit: ko hi śakto raṇe pārtha pāñcālānāṃ mahārathau bhīṣmadroṇau yudhā jetuṃ śakratulyaparākramau
english: For who among the Pāñcālas, O Pārtha, was able to vanquish in battle by force of arms those two great chariot-warriors, Bhīṣma and Droṇa, equal in valor to Śakra?

sanskrit: ko hi śāṃtanavaṃ saṃkhye droṇaṃ vaikartanaṃ kṛpam drauṇiṃ ca saumadattiṃ ca kṛtavarmāṇam eva ca saindhavaṃ madrarājaṃ ca rājānaṃ ca suyodhanam
english: For who, in the clash of battle, could face the son of Śaṃtanu, Droṇa, Vaikartana, Kṛpa, the son of Droṇa, the son of Somadatta, and Kṛtavarman too, the lord of the Sindhus, the king of the Madras, and King Suyodhana —

sanskrit: vīrān kṛtāstrān samare sarvān evānuvartinaḥ akṣauhiṇīpatīn ugrān saṃrabdhān yuddhadurmadān
english: all those heroes, accomplished in arms in battle, each with his followers, fierce commanders of armies, furious and mad with the lust of war?

sanskrit: śreṇyaś ca bahulāḥ kṣīṇāḥ pradīrṇāśvarathadvipāḥ nānājanapadāś cogrāḥ kṣatriyāṇām amarṣiṇām
english: And many companies have been brought low, their horses, chariots, and elephants torn asunder — fierce hosts from divers lands, of warriors who would brook no offense.

sanskrit: govāsadāsamīyānāṃ vasātīnāṃ ca bhārata vrātyānāṃ vāṭadhānānāṃ bhojānāṃ cāpi māninām
english: Of the Govāsas, the Dāsamīyas, and the Vasātis, O Bhārata, of the Vrātyas, the Vāṭadhānas, and the proud Bhojas as well —

sanskrit: udīrṇāś ca mahāsenā brahmakṣatrasya bhārata tvāṃ samāsādya nidhanaṃ gatāḥ sāśvarathadvipāḥ
english: and the swelling great hosts of the brāhmaṇa-warriors, O Bhārata, having met you, went to their destruction, together with their horses, chariots, and elephants.

sanskrit: ugrāś ca krūrakarmāṇas tukhārā yavanāḥ khaśāḥ dārvābhisārā daradāḥ śakā ramaṭhataṅgaṇāḥ
english: And the fierce, cruel-doing Tukhāras, Yavanas, and Khaśas, the Dārvābhisāras, Daradas, Śakas, Ramaṭhas, and Taṅgaṇas,

sanskrit: andhrakāś ca pulindāś ca kirātāś cogravikramāḥ mlecchāś ca pārvatīyāś ca sāgarānūpavāsinaḥ saṃrambhiṇo yuddhaśauṇḍā balino dṛbdhapāṇayaḥ
english: and the Andhrakas and Pulindas, the Kirātas of fierce prowess, and the Mlecchas and the mountain-dwellers, and those who dwell by the sea and its marshlands — wrathful, drunk with battle, mighty, with steadfast hands —

sanskrit: ete suyodhanasyārthe saṃrabdhāḥ kurubhiḥ saha na śakyā yudhi nirjetuṃ tvad anyena paraṃtapa
english: these, raging for Suyodhana's sake together with the Kurus, could be conquered in battle by none other than you, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭram udagraṃ hi vyūḍhaṃ dṛṣṭvā mahābalam yasya tvaṃ na bhaves trātā pratīyāt ko nu mānavaḥ
english: For seeing the host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son towering and arrayed in mighty strength, what man, whose protector you were not, would dare advance against it?

sanskrit: tat sāgaram ivoddhūtaṃ rajasā saṃvṛtaṃ balam vidārya pāṇḍavaiḥ kruddhais tvayā guptair hataṃ vibho
english: That army, surging like the ocean and veiled in dust, was rent asunder and slain by the wrathful Pāṇḍavas guarded by you, O lord.

sanskrit: māgadhānām adhipatir jayatseno mahābalaḥ adya saptaiva cāhāni hataḥ saṃkhye 'bhimanyunā
english: The lord of the Māgadhas, the mighty Jayatsena, was slain in battle by Abhimanyu just seven days ago this day.

sanskrit: tato daśa sahasrāṇi gajānāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām jaghāna gadayā bhīmas tasya rājñaḥ paricchadam tato 'nye 'pi hatā nāgā rathāś ca śataśo balāt
english: Then ten thousand elephants of terrible deeds, that king's retinue, Bhīma slew with his mace; and other elephants too were slain, and chariots by the hundred, by his might.

sanskrit: tad evaṃ samare tāta vartamāne mahābhaye bhīmasenaṃ samāsādya tvāṃ ca pāṇḍava kauravāḥ savājirathanāgāś ca mṛtyulokam ito gatāḥ
english: Thus, dear one, as that great and dreadful battle raged on, the Kauravas, encountering Bhīmasena and you, O Pāṇḍava, went from here to the realm of Death, together with their horses, chariots, and elephants.

sanskrit: tathā senāmukhe tatra nihate pārtha pāṇḍavaiḥ bhīṣmaḥ prāsṛjad ugrāṇi śaravarṣāṇi māriṣa
english: And when the van of the army there had been struck down by the Pāṇḍavas, O Pārtha, Bhīṣma loosed fierce showers of arrows, O venerable one.

sanskrit: sa cedikāśipāñcālān karūṣān matsyakekayān śaraiḥ pracchādya nidhanam anayat paruṣāstravit
english: Covering with his arrows the Cedis, the Kāśis, the Pāñcālas, the Karūṣas, the Matsyas, and the Kekayas, that knower of cruel weapons led them to their destruction.

sanskrit: tasya cāpacyutair bāṇaiḥ paradehavidāraṇaiḥ pūrṇam ākāśam abhavad rukmapuṅkhair ajihmagaiḥ
english: And with the arrows loosed from his bow, the rippers of the bodies of foes, gold-feathered and flying straight, the whole sky was filled.
